title: Watchtower handback tally — 2028-10-02
content:
Shift: Night watch (20:00–04:00 PDT) — Aisha Patel handing to Luca Moretti (next on-call).
Time zone: PDT (UTC-7).

Summary (high level):
- Two notable events during the shift. The primary event was a regional latency spike affecting hosted inference in us-west-2 between ~03:12–03:47 UTC. Secondary was a routing configuration flapping for a small set of Private deployment tenants during a planned deploy window (limited impact).
- No customer-facing incidents escalated to account teams, but alert noise increased and one internal PagerDuty page (PD-INC-90732) was triggered and resolved before escalation to on-call engineer rotation.

Incident A — us-west-2 inference latency spike (major focus)
- Window: 2028-10-02 03:12–03:47 UTC (observed in Grafana panel 'inference-latency', dashboard link above).
- Symptoms: 95th percentile token latency rose from baseline ~180ms to ~720ms; tail tokens >1s for heavy-context requests. Error rate (service 5xx) rose from 0.02% to 0.6%. Autoscaler churn seen in same time window.
- Immediate mitigations taken:
  1) Put autoscaling to manual +1 instance to stop churn (temporary).
 2) Routed a subset of traffic to the quantized model variant (fallback route) for latency-sensitive routes.
  3) Disabled continuous KV cache eviction job on the affected pool (suspected noisy eviction).
  4) Warmed caches with synthetic prefix requests for top 20 routes.
- Timeline (concise):
  03:12 — First alert: p95 > 400ms on hosted-api/us-west-2.
  03:16 — Correlated with spike in 'kv_cache_eviction_rate' on the pool.
  03:20 — Autoscaler started thrashing (scale up/down loops).
  03:25 — Manual scale +1 applied; eviction job paused.
  03:31 — Traffic routing to quantized variant for 10% of requests.
  03:40 — p95 trending down; by 03:47 metrics back to baseline.
- Root cause hypothesis (current): Metric miscalculation in the autoscaler hook combined with increased KV cache eviction activity caused repeated cold-cache startups leading to tail latency. The autoscaler was responding to a noisy metric (cache eviction rate) as if it were request queue depth.
- Evidence collected: Grafana panels (latency, eviction_rate, instance_count), infra logs showing repeated restart events, pod logs with 'cache miss' flood, and the autoscaler debug trace (attached in SRE-4217).
- Current blocking items: PR to fix autoscaler metric filter (PR: https://git.redwood.internal/redwood/infra/pull/1284) is open; change hasn't been rolled to prod.
- Post-shift next steps (actionable):
  - SRE-4217: finish autoscaler metric filter + unit tests (owner: Ravi Shah, due 2028-10-05).
  - Add an alert for 'cache_eviction_rate > threshold AND sustained p95 increase' to avoid autoscaler reacting to eviction noise (owner: Chen Li, ticket SRE-4228).
  - Update runbook section 'recovering-from-cache-thrash' with explicit temporary mitigations (pause eviction job, manual scale, route to quantized variant). Draft below.

Incident B — Private routing flapping during config push (low impact)
- Window: 2028-10-02 01:05–01:22 UTC (during a scheduled config rollout to a subset of Private controllers).
- Symptoms: Brief 502/503s for 3 tenants on private VPC controllers due to a mis-ordered config apply (routing table updated before backend readiness check).
- Mitigation: Immediate rollback of config for the affected controllers; follow-up deploy with readiness gating.
- Action items:
  - Create a pre-deploy checklist for private controller config changes (owner: Ravi Shah, SRE-4230).
  - Add a gating job to CI that validates readiness probe passes before routing updates (owner: Platform Eng).

Runbook draft — 'recovering-from-cache-thrash' (skeleton / please refine):
- Purpose: Steps to stabilize inference pools experiencing repeated cold-cache evictions and autoscaler churn.
- Preconditions: Access to Grafana, kubectl cluster for the pool, autoscaler logs, and traffic routing controls in Console.
- Steps:
  1) Identify affected pool(s) via Grafana panel 'pool-token-p95' and 'kv_cache_eviction_rate'.
  2) Temporarily set autoscaler.mode = manual (scale to +1 instance above baseline).
  3) Pause any scheduled cache-eviction/compaction jobs (name pattern: cache-evict-*).
  4) Launch targeted synthetic warmers for top N routes (script: infra/scripts/warm-prefixes.sh).
  5) If p95 does not improve within 8 minutes, route 10–20% of latency-sensitive traffic to quantized or smaller-context variant via routing policy.
  6) Collect logs: autoscaler trace, pod logs, eviction metrics, instance count timeline; attach to SRE ticket.
  7) After stable state, revert autoscaler to autoscale mode and monitor for 30 minutes.
- Notes: Need to document exact CLI commands and Console locations; I left placeholders in steps 2 and 3.

Deferred / follow-ups (things I didn't finish):
- Flesh out CLI snippets in the runbook and add exact Console navigation steps (TODO: me, Aisha — due 2028-10-04).
- Create SLO post-incident note with customer-facing impact summary if required (decide after SRE-4217 conclusion).
- Validate the autoscaler fix in staging with synthetic eviction noise generator (Luca Moretti to coordinate, target 2028-10-06).

Operational notes & observations (informal):
- FYI: During the spike, the 'tokenizer' pod logs showed repeated deallocation warnings which might indicate memory pressure on heavyweight models when caches are cold — worth a quick memory-profile (Chen Li).
- The synthetic warmers script needs rate-limiting to avoid creating load storms; added a comment in infra repo but didn't open a PR.
- Slack thread: see channel thread (linked above). There are a few quick-blame anchors (kinda noisy) — silo communication looked fine.

Open tickets referenced:
- SRE-4217 (primary autoscaler investigation)
- SRE-4228 (alert tuning for eviction+latency)
- SRE-4230 (private deploy pre-checklist)
- PD-INC-90732 (PagerDuty incident record, closed)

Checks completed before handoff:
- Confirmed p95 back to baseline on hosted-api/us-west-2.
- Confirmed eviction job remains paused (note: this is a temporary mitigation; must be resumed once fix is live).
- Confirmed PR 1284 exists (needs review/CI passing).

Handoff ask for next on-call (Luca):
- Keep autoscaler in manual mode until SRE-4217 PR is merged and deployed to prod, unless scaling is required for customer SLA (call me first).
- If you see a new p95 increase >2x baseline and eviction_rate is low, escalate immediately to infra on-call.
- Please follow up with Platform Eng on adding readiness gating for private controller config changes (SRE-4230).

Notes to self (Aisha):
- Remember to attach autoscaler debug traces to SRE-4217 before EOD.
- Start a short retrospective note in Confluence summarizing the timeline and include a small appendix on metrics and graphs.

Quick links & artifacts (again):
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/abcd/inference-latency
- PagerDuty: PD-INC-90732
- Ticket: SRE-4217 (autoscaler), SRE-4228, SRE-4230
- PR: https://git.redwood.internal/redwood/infra/pull/1284
- Slack: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C0SRE/p1234567890

End of shift checklist:
- [x] Metrics stabilized? Yes
- [x] Eviction job paused? Yes (temp)
- [ ] PR merged and deployed? No
- [ ] Runbook CLI snippets updated? No

If anything looks off during Luca's watch, @me on Slack and I'll jump in. Thanks and good handover.

-- Aisha
